note: Window agent p0400-p0499, 2 Nov 2026. Fixes: Tuyuhun 426-438 drawn as the 173-cell delta; Vandals 429-434 drawn over Western Sahara; Ostrogoths kept in the Balkans through 489; Gaul unowned at the end of 407; Northern Wei lost Henan, Jining and the Ordos at its 426/439/441/451/476 keyframes. Review 2 Nov 2026 (p0400-p0499 reviewer): keyframe_overrides/0 starts in 430 (no 426 snap); the Jining disc (Liu Song's Yan Province) taken out of keyframe_overrides/5-7 and given to Liu Song 439-465 by keyframe_overrides/10-11 and rulings/0.

region.text: Epirus (settled 479) and the Lower Danube in Moesia: the Balkan land the Ostrogoths left when Theodoric 'moved with his people towards Italy in the autumn of 488'

events.note: 488: Theodoric leaves the Balkans. 'Theodoric then moved with his people towards Italy in the autumn of 488.' The dossier closes the two vassal relations in 488 but never takes the land away, so the ostrogoths_480 shape (Epirus and Moesia) stays drawn through 489 beside the Italian campaign and claims cells the Eastern Roman Empire holds (718 cell-years of conflict 489-490).

region.text: Qing and Ji Provinces, the whole of Shandong: 'annexing those provinces for Northern Wei' in spring 468 (the ledger's 468 gain draws only a 150 km disc round Weifang)

events.note: 468: Wei annexes Qing and Ji Provinces. 'Murong Baiyao forced Cui's surrender in spring 468' and captured Shen Wenxiu's post at Dongyang, 'annexing those provinces for Northern Wei'. The northern-wei_451 keyframe cuts all of Shandong for Liu Song until 466-468 and the 466 and 468 gain events draw only discs (Xuzhou, Jining, Weifang), so 214 cells of Shandong belong to nobody for 468-475 until the 476 keyframe takes them.

correction.text: the whole 426 shape (316,763 km2, to 34.2 N and 103.7 E), drawn from 430, not 426: 426-429 keep what Tuyuhun held in 425 (no keyframe snaps in those years)

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier's 426 correction was Cliopatria's 426 shape minus its 414 shape, the 173 added cells only, so Tuyuhun was drawn as that sliver for 426-438 (929 cells dropped at 426, 1,114 re-added at 439). The note says 426-429 keep the 414 shape and the 426 shape starts in 430: 'Meanwhile, the rest of Qin's territory was conquered by the Tuyuhun, leaving Mumo with only a lone city' (Western Qin page, in its 430 passage). [Review 2 Nov 2026: the 414 shape re-snapped in 426 took 86 cells of the Huangshui valley (Xining) from Western Qin and 48 cells from Northern Liang in 426, four years before the page's 430 conquest; the keyframe now starts in 430 (the same shape as tuyuhun_430), so 426-429 keep the 425 holdings.]

correction.text: the whole 426 shape (316,763 km2, to 34.2 N and 103.7 E), drawn from 430: the 414 land plus the rest of Western Qin's territory

keyframe_overrides.why: New keyframe for 430-438 (replaces the delta-only tuyuhun_426 correction for those years): 'the rest of Qin's territory was conquered by the Tuyuhun, leaving Mumo with only a lone city' (Western Qin page, 430); Mumo surrendered in 431. The ledger's 430 gain (426 shape minus 414 shape) now adds nothing new.

correction.text: the Roman land of Mauretania and Numidia (the part inside the Western Roman Empire's 426 shape), without Hippo Regius until its fall in 432

keyframe_overrides.why: The region name 'Mauretania' resolves to the whole of modern Morocco including Western Sahara (3,121 cells drawn from 429, 2,664 more than the ledger's own gain from the Western Roman Empire). The page has the Vandals 'conquering the coastal regions of what is now Tunisia, and Algeria' in 429 and settling 'in the provinces of Numidia and Mauretania' in 435 ('coastal Numidia and parts of Mauretania'), and says nothing of Morocco's Atlantic coast or the Sahara. Cut to the Roman provinces' land, the same cells the western-roman-empire dossier gives away (241 cells).

correction.text: Britain and Gaul as the Western Roman Empire held them in 406: Constantine crossed the Channel at Bononia in 407

keyframe_overrides.why: western-roman-empire_407 already takes Britain and Gaul from Honorius in 407 (2,486 cells), but Constantine's 407 keyframe held Britain only, so Gaul belonged to nobody at the end of 407 and Constantine received it in 408. The page has him acclaimed in Britain in early 407 and then 'He crossed the Channel at Bononia (modern Boulogne)'; Arles was his capital 'By May 408'. The page does not date the end of 407 exactly: soft.

Wei took Tongwancheng on 11 July 427 (Xia page, 'the Battle of Tongwancheng'; the city 'served as a frontier garrison until the Song dynasty'), regained all the lands south of the Yellow River by spring 431, and Liu Song's 450 attack on Wei aimed 'again hoping to regain the provinces south of the Yellow River' (Taiwu page). region.text: Yan Province (Xiaqiu, modern Yanzhou in Jining), western Shandong

rulings.why: Liu Song's 'Yan (modern western Shandong)' province was raided by Wei in spring 446, but 'Northern Wei forces did not capture or hold those provinces' (Taiwu page); its governor Bi Zhongjing went over to Wei only in 466 (Emperor Ming page). The northern-wei_426 keyframe (426-438) still holds the disc from the 423 gain, so Liu Song's 439 keyframe needs this ruling to take it back; no page dates the return between 423 and 446 (soft). Added by the reviewer of p0400-p0499.
